The format of Boot Progress Code is:
- 4 bytes EFI_STATUS_CODE_TYPE
  + 1 Byte STATUS_CODE_TYPE
  + 2 Bytes STATUS_CODE_RESERVED
  + 1 Byte STATUS_CODE_SEVERITY (It seems that DEN0069E_SBMR_2.1 is wrong when talk this field is 2bytes)
- 4 Bytes EFI_STATUS_CODE_VALUE
  + 2 bytes EFI_STATUS_CODE_OPERATION
  + 1 byte EFI_STATUS_CODE_SUBCLASS
  + 1 byte EFI_STATUS_CODE_CLASS
- 1 Byte Instance

you should split 9 bytes of data into smaller input parameters (maybe 7 input parameters) as I mentiond above. E.g: https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-host-ipmid/blob/master/dcmihandler.cpp#L399
This is simply intended to verify the boot progress code in a single step and update BootStateObject below.
IMO, it makes reviewer difficult to understand all cases of the `data`. If you split `data` into 7 parameters, it is easy to understand the purpose of each parameter.
You should check each EFI_STATUS_CODE_TYPE/EFI_STATUS_CODE_VALUE/Instance data instead all of data at same time. I think you can remove sbmrBootProgressStages
Do you see any potential issues with checking all the data at once? It will be simplify for code maintenance and readability.

I don't think your code is simple for code maintenance. When I see to the `sbmrBootProgressStages`, I don't know where are those key come from.
